summary: @onereach/channel-transformer preinstall drops Bun runtime to execute obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares `"preinstall": "node setup.mjs"`. setup.mjs is itself obfuscated with hex-mangled identifiers (`_0x488df8`, `_0x52943e`, string-property dictionaries) and, on install, downloads the Bun runtime binary for the installer's platform from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/<platform>.zip`, extracts it to a temp directory, marks it executable, and then invokes it via `execFileSync(bun, [<tmp>/math_init.js],...)` against a 727KB single-line bundled file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is heavily obfuscated with a rotating string-array cipher (`function WV8StW(...) {... MmgoCP.push(MmgoCP.shift())... }` over a ~1500-entry constant table) and hex-mangled globals; it is not source-mapped and not documented. The package is advertised as a channel data-model transformer for Slack/Teams/Generic messaging formats, a pure data-transformation library with no legitimate need for a second language runtime or an opaque executable payload at install time. Using Bun rather than the already-present Node interpreter to run the obfuscated bundle evades scanners that only inspect Node-resolved code paths, and the obfuscation makes the payload's behavior unverifiable prior to execution on the installer's machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
